subject: System Design
title: Lamport Clocks
description: A quick, practical guide to Lamport Clocks.

hook.text: Leslie Lamport asked: can we order events without synchronized physical clocks? The answer changed everything.

buildup.text: A Lamport clock is a logical counter. Each node increments it on every event and sends it with messages.

discovery.text: If event A happened before B, then A's Lamport timestamp is lower. Causal ordering is preserved.

twist.text: Two events with equal Lamport timestamps might be concurrent — or not. Lamport clocks can't tell the difference.

climax.text: Lamport clocks give a total order that's consistent with causality — a foundation of distributed systems theory.

punchline.text: Logical clocks order events without physical time.

quiz.question: What do Lamport clocks provide?
options: A total order of events consistent with causality
